name: Stephen
overview: Stephen was a male believer chosen to serve the widows of the Hellenistic Jews in the early church, highlighting his role in practical ministry. Scripture does not specify his tribal affiliation or additional personal details. His selection to this service demonstrates the early church's commitment to caring for all members, especially those in need.
namesAndTitles: Stephen is the only recorded name for this individual, with no specific meaning or divine origin noted in the biblical text. The name itself is presented plainly without additional significance attached in the scriptural reference.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record family relationships for Stephen beyond his role serving the widows of the Hellenistic Jews. There is no mention of relatives or other personal connections in the biblical account.
scriptureSignificance: Stephen holds a pivotal place in the New Testament as the first Christian martyr, chosen to serve in the early church and empowered by faith and the Holy Spirit to perform miracles. His bold defense before the Jewish council and his vision of Jesus standing at God's right hand affirm Christ's ongoing advocacy for His followers. Stephen's death marked the beginning of intensified persecution against the church and contributed to the wider spread of the gospel.
